title: (RHEA-2012:1477) Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise 1.0 Client Release Advisory
portal_summary:
OpenShift Enterprise is a cloud computing Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) solution
from Red Hat, and is designed for on-premise or private cloud deployments.
Unlike an Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) solution, which provides on-demand
access to raw compute resources, or a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution,
which provides on-demand access to a complete application, OpenShift Enterprise,
as a PaaS, enables on-demand access to a cloud-based application platform so
that enterprises can easily build their applications and run them in a cloud
architecture. OpenShift Enterprise automates much of the provisioning and
systems management of the application platform stack. This allows the IT
Operations team to meet the growing demand for new application services coming
from the business more easily.

OpenShift Enterprise also provides an on-demand, elastic, scalable, and fully
configured application development, testing, and hosting environment. This way,
application developers can focus on doing what they do best, coding these new
application services. Once installed in a data center or a private cloud,
OpenShift Enterprise provides a self-service capability for developers to create
scalable applications in the PaaS easily. Developers can begin coding the
application using their favorite development environment, with their choice of
programming language and middleware.

This update includes the following RPMs:
rhc-0.99.11-1.el6op.noarch.rpm
rubygem-commander-4.0.3-4.el6op.noarch.rpm

Note: The following RPMS are common to the Client and Infrastructure channels,
but are only in the Infrastructure Errata release report. The RPMS are:

portal_solution:
Before applying this update, make sure you have applied all previously released
errata intended for your system.

To update all RPMs for your particular architecture, run the following command:

rpm -Fvh [filenames]

where [filenames] is a list of the RPMs you wish to upgrade. Only the RPMs
installed on your system will be updated. If the RPMs that are included in the
list are not installed on your system, they will not be updated. Note that you
can also use wildcards (*.rpm) if your current directory *only* contains the
desired RPMs. Please note that this update is also available via Red Hat
Network, which many people find easier to use for applying updates. 

To use Red Hat Network, launch the Red Hat Update Agent with the following
command:

up2date

An interactive process will start, and the appropriate RPMs will be upgraded on
your system.
portal_description:
OpenShift Enterprise includes the following functionality:

Polyglot Language Support – OpenShift Enterprise includes built-in support for Java, Ruby, Python, PHP and Perl programming languages.  Developers can choose the language that suits their own skills, or the requirements of the job.

Multiple Interfaces – OpenShift Enterprise also allows developers to work the way they want to work by providing multiple interfaces to the PaaS. Developers can use a rich set of command-line tools, a powerful web console, which can be accessed on multiple devices, or an Eclipse-based Integrated Development Environment, such as JBoss Developer Studio.

Autoscaling – OpenShift Enterprise can scale applications automatically to handle increased traffic and demand on the application.

Application Portability – OpenShift Enterprise is built with standard language and middleware run-times so that any application written on OpenShift can easily be moved to another environment that supports similar programming languages. OpenShift Enterprise provides developers with the flexibility to choose their environment.

Open Source – OpenShift Enterprise is based on open source technologies.  The OpenShift PaaS itself is derived from the OpenShift Origin open source project.

Built on Red Hat Technologies – OpenShift Enterprise is built on Red Hat's time-tested and enterprise class open source technology stack, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux and JBoss Enterprise Application Platform.
